chunks: And from him, from Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Amir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Al-Fadala, from Aban, from Al-Zurari, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who prayed the morning prayer at night, deceived by the moon from that, and slept until the sun rose, and was informed that he had prayed at night, he said: 'He must repeat his prayer.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one prays Fajr early due to moonlight and sleeps until sunrise?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ruling for *salat al-ta'ajjul* (praying early due to mistaken timing), establishing that if one prays Fajr while the moon is still visible and subsequently sleeps until sunrise, the prayer is valid but must be repeated to ensure it is performed within its proper time window. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the precise definition of prayer times (*awqat*) and the importance of correcting errors in timing to maintain the validity of obligatory acts. It reflects the practical jurisprudence (*fiqh*) derived from the Ahl al-Bayt, ensuring that the spiritual integrity of the prayer is preserved even when human error occurs.
